title: Redwood discovery - model selection - Polaris Analytics
summary: Initial model-selection discovery: customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for multilingual, long-context (32k+) pipelines and tool-calling. Discussed open models (Llama 3, Mistral, Falcon), quantization, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC) and next-step pilot/benchmarks.
transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2027-05-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rina (Polaris Head of ML), Marcus (Platform), Tanya (CTO)

--- Summary (auto):
Quick discovery on model selection and deployment mode. Customer needs: multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), 32k+ context for long-doc summarization and multi-turn tool calls to their internal APIs. Concerned about latency and unit cost; want SOC2 + KMS + VPC for production.

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through model selection and deployment options - hosted, dedicated or private - and figure out the fit for polaris.
00:12 Rina: thanks, yeah we have some background. Current stack is a mix of open-source inference on-prem for research and a small managed api for experiments, but nothing production. main things: summarization of long financial docs up to ~50k tokens, multi-lingual extraction, and also tool calling to our internal pricing API.
00:32 Ethan: ok got it. when you say 50k tokens is that peak single-request context or do you chunk and stitch?
00:38 Rina: we currently chunk but want to move to a single long-context pipeline if feasible - ideally 32k to 64k native context. we can compromise at 32k for a pilot.
00:50 Marcus: latency is important - product needs sub-500ms first-token ideally for short queries, but for long-doc summarization higher latency is ok. cost is also a big factor, can't be 10x of current per-token.
01:05 Sofia: that's a common tradeoff. for 32k+ context, we usually recommend either dedicated capacity on GPU for predictable throughput or private deployment if you need full data isolation. hosted is fastest to get started and cheaper for lower volume.
01:18 Tanya: security wise we need SOC2 type 2, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs and customer-managed KMS. can you support VPC peering / private link?
01:30 Ethan: yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and KMS integration; Dedicated also supports VPC and brings reserved capacity. Hosted API supports SOC2 and encrypted at rest but for strict data residency and KMS you likely look at private or dedicated with private networking options.
01:45 Rina: model-wise, we are curious about open models - we've benchmarked Llama 3 70B and Mistral large variants. want to understand accuracy for instruction-following, multilingual performance and tool-calling / function-calling behaviour.
01:58 Sofia: great. common choices we see: Llama-family (Llama 3 variants) for strong instruction tuning; Mistral (small/large) which is cost-effective and often fast; Falcon for some workloads; and our curated quantized variants for lower-cost inference. do you have a preference based on your evals?
02:12 Rina: Llama 3 was good on english summarization but struggled a bit on Spanish edge cases. Mistral 7B-instruct was surprisingly good but we need large-context behaviour.
02:26 Ethan: technical note - long-context behavior depends on model architecture and runtime support. Redwood runtime has optimized kernels and KV cache management; our dedicated/private options can support 32k or 64k contexts depending on the model and quantization profile. quantization sometimes reduces context performance slightly but gives big cost wins.
02:45 Marcus: can you do tool-calling / function calling reliably? we need to call internal pricing and legal-check APIs during multi-turn flows.
02:54 Ethan: yes, we support function/tool calling and structured outputs. important to test with your exact API patterns - sometimes models hallucinate parameter names if not constrained. we also offer request-level policies and tracer hooks so you can see arguments and fallbacks.
03:10 Rina: what about latency on 32k windows? and batch sizes?
03:16 Ethan: for large contexts, latency is dominated by model forward passes; with dedicated GPUs we typically see 2x-3x faster latency vs shared hosted for the same batch. caching/prefix KV can reduce repeated context cost. if you need first-token under 500ms on short queries, hosted small models or dedicated small-profile nodes are fine. for 32k summarization, expect multi-second responses - can be async or streamed.
03:37 Tanya: any customers doing hybrid - hosted for dev and dedicated/private for prod?
03:41 Sofia: yes, that's very common. start hosted to iterate, then move to dedicated for predictable throughput and cost, or private when you need strict network/isolation controls.
03:52 Rina: about multilingual - do you advise fine-tuning or instruction prompts?
03:56 Ethan: often a mixture: prompt-engineering and targeted finetune on domain text. some models have better base multilingual coverage (Mistral variants have decent multilingual behavior, Llama 3 improved too). we can run comparative evals on your Spanish and French test sets.
04:12 Marcus: what's the typical cost delta between full float vs 8-bit quant vs int4?
04:18 Ethan: roughly, int8/int4 quantization can reduce inference cost 2-4x depending on throughput, with some accuracy tradeoff. it varies by model - some architectures quantize better. Redwood Optimize provides recommendations per workload.
04:33 Rina: security again - audit logs and retention, can we control retention windows?
04:38 Ethan: yes, on Dedicated and Private you can configure retention and audit log exports, and integrate with your SIEM. Hosted has standard retention but we can discuss enterprise packages.
04:50 Sofia: ok wrapping to priorities - sounds like main asks: run benchmarks (Llama3 70B, Mistral large, our quantized variants) on 32k pipeline, evaluate multilingual accuracy, and validate tool-calling reliability and latency.
05:05 Rina: correct. also bring pricing for hosted vs dedicated vs private (estimates for 50k tokens/day baseline).
05:12 Sofia: noted. we'll propose a pilot: 2-week benchmark with dedicated nodes + sample hosted runs, and a security pack doc.
05:20 Marcus: timeline - we want a pilot in June if possible. stakeholders for procurement will be Tanya + infra.
05:28 Tanya: procurement will need SOC2 artifacts and contract terms; also legal wants indemnity language - we'll loop them after the pilot scope.
05:38 Ethan: one more technical quirk - for large-context single-request summarization we recommend testing both native long-context models and chunk+retrieval pipeline to compare quality and cost. sometimes chunked with semantic retrieval is cheaper with similar quality.
05:55 Rina: good point - we do have a vector DB (pinecone) but would prefer to avoid extra hops if native context suffices.
06:04 Sofia: next steps recap in the minute: we'll send pricing + security docs; Ethan to run benchmarks and share results; schedule a technical deep dive for model fitting next week. any other items?
06:18 Marcus: can you include sample throughput numbers for 32k on 1x A100 vs 8x A100?
06:25 Ethan: yes will include rough numbers and a benchmark plan.
06:30 Tanya: we'll share a short eval dataset (spanish/english legal summaries + tool-calling examples).
06:36 Sofia: perfect - thanks all, we'll follow up with the pilot proposal and calendar invites.

--- End transcript
